card.name: Zaouli
card.tagline: Guro masked solo dance honouring feminine beauty
card.profile: Zaouli is a masked solo dance of the Guro people of central Cote d'Ivoire (Bouafle and Zuenoula areas), created in the 1950s and named after a girl, 'Djela Lou Zaouli.' Per UNESCO, which inscribed it in 2017, it unites sculpture (the wooden mask), weaving (the costume), music and dance; a single male dancer, his upper body almost still beneath a striped costume, executes dazzlingly rapid, never-repeated footwork to flutes and drums. The mask is sacred, carved over days from yaranza wood, and only trained initiates may wear it.
card.insight: Zaouli is celebrated as one of the world's most technically demanding dances and a unifying emblem of Guro and Ivorian identity; it gained national fame as a favourite of President Felix Houphouet-Boigny (UNESCO; Wikipedia).
